title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
headnote: KESCO's writ against an Electricity Ombudsman order levying a Supply Code 7.1 fine of Rs 50 per day on the Executive Engineer for a three-year delay in replacing a meter after the consumer deposited the change-of-meter fee was dismissed. Findings of fact on deposit and delayed replacement, and the Commission's consequential action under the Code, were left undisturbed.
facts: The consumer deposited the fee for change of the electricity supply meter on 4 March 2008. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company did not replace the meter until 22 March 2011, a delay of nearly three years. By order dated 4 January 2012 the Electricity Ombudsman recorded those facts and, under Electricity Supply Code clause 7.1, levied a fine of Rs 50 per day on the Executive Engineer. The company challenged that order and the U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission's consequential action in this writ petition.

holding_units.holding: Findings of fact that the change-of-meter fee was deposited on 4 March 2008 and the meter replaced only on 22 March 2011 after nearly three years admit of no interference; consequential action under Electricity Supply Code 7.1, including the Rs 50 per day fine on the Executive Engineer for that delay, does not warrant interference.
